Compact change review

validator-fix-1 (F1)

Correct chain ownership for arbToGnosis claimer reads and finality checks.

Compared: fix/val-doc-1...task/validator-fix-1 · 3 files · +139/−8 · commits d105e59, 76fbd7f

  • TL;DR
  • What changed per file
  • Review verdict & residual findings

TL;DR

The arbToGnosis path spans three chains: inbox on Arbitrum Sepolia, router on Sepolia, and outbox on Chiado. The old claimer reused the router/Sepolia finalized block number for Chiado contract reads. Since block numbers have meaning only on their own chain, that could point the stateRoot read and Claimed scan at the wrong place and prevent a valid claim.

This patch separates the two responsibilities:

  • Sepolia router provider remains the L1 anchor for Arbitrum batch/finality checks.
  • Chiado outbox provider now supplies the finalized head, lookback floor, and range used to read the outbox.
Bottom line: the implementation matches the stated F1 fix. Static review found no blocking defect.

What changed per file

validator-cli/src/helpers/claimer.ts

Core fix makeClaim now receives both providers explicitly: the real outbox provider and queryRpc, where queryRpc = veaRouterProvider ?? veaOutboxProvider.

const queryRpc = veaRouterProvider ?? veaOutboxProvider;

// Finality: Arbitrum batches are checked against their L1 posting chain.
fetchSettledReadBlocks({
  inboxProvider: transactionHandler.veaInboxProvider,
  outboxProvider: queryRpc,
  ...
});

// Outbox reads: block numbers come from the outbox's own chain.
const outboxHeadBlock = await veaOutboxProvider.getBlock("finalized");
await veaOutbox.stateRoot({ blockTag: outboxHeadBlock.number });

const floorBlock = await getLookbackFloorBlock({
  provider: veaOutboxProvider,
  chainId,
  epochPeriod,
});
findLatestLog({ fromBlock: floorBlock, toBlock: outboxHeadBlock.number, ... });

Why: on chain ID 10200, queryRpc is Sepolia and veaOutboxProvider is Chiado. The former is correct for proving where Arbitrum posted its batches; the latter is the only valid source of block tags and log ranges for the Chiado outbox. For arbToEth, the router is absent and the fallback preserves the existing single-L1 behavior.

Important semantic shift: settledBlocks.outboxBlock is still returned by the finality helper, but the claimer no longer uses it to address the outbox. On arbToGnosis that value belongs to the router chain, despite the legacy field name.

validator-cli/src/watcher.ts

Wiring fix The watcher adds veaRouterProvider to CheckAndClaimParams.

const checkAndClaimParams: CheckAndClaimParams = {
  ...,
  veaOutboxProvider,
  veaRouterProvider,
  veaOutbox,
  ...
};

Why: the provider was already constructed from routerRPC and passed to validator/challenger logic, but not to the claimer. Without this line, checkAndClaim falls back to the Chiado outbox provider and asks the Arbitrum SDK to perform its L1 finality work against the wrong chain. The change makes the production call path agree with the helper’s existing provider-selection logic.

validator-cli/src/helpers/claimer.test.ts

Regression coverage The tests introduce chain ID 10200 cases with deliberately different provider objects and block-number scales.

  • The settled-read test now expects stateRoot at the outbox provider’s finalized block (999), not the finality helper’s router block (555).
  • A Chiado/Sepolia test uses a 30,000,000 outbox head and 7,000,000 router head, then checks that the state read and every Claimed range stay on the Chiado scale.
  • A second chain-10200 test invokes the real resolveSettledReadBlocks with a mocked finality function and checks provider identity: Sepolia router is L1, Arbitrum inbox is L2, and Chiado remains the outbox read source.

Why: distinct objects and non-overlapping block scales make accidental provider substitution visible; mocks with identical shapes or block numbers could let the original bug pass.

Review verdict + residual findings

Approve — no blocking findings in the reviewed diff.

The provider split is coherent at the helper boundary, the production watcher now supplies the router provider, the arbToEth fallback remains intact, and the tests exercise both sides of the split. git diff --check also passes.

Residual findings

  • Low — redundant unpinned read remains. checkAndClaim still calls veaOutbox.stateRoot() before choosing the devnet/testnet branch. In testnet claim flow that value is discarded and replaced by the new finalized Chiado read. This is pre-existing, does not reintroduce cross-chain block tags, and does not affect the decision value; however, it adds an unnecessary latest-state RPC dependency and could be cleaned up by moving the read into the devnet branch.
  • Low — watcher propagation is not directly tested. The new finality test manually supplies veaRouterProvider to checkAndClaim. It strongly covers helper behavior, but no watcher-level test asserts that processEpochsForNetwork forwards the constructed router provider. The one-line production wiring was verified statically.
  • Clarity — legacy naming. The finality API calls its L1 parameter/result “outbox” even when it is the Sepolia router for arbToGnosis. The new comments explain this, but a later rename could reduce future chain-mixing risk.
Verification boundary: Jest was not executed because this review was constrained to read-only Git inspection. The verdict is based on the complete diff, surrounding provider/finality/lookback code, route configuration, and static whitespace validation.

Refs reviewed: fix/val-doc-1 → task/validator-fix-1.
